overall: The AG found the Committee as a whole violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a quorum about public business (five of seven emails), though not intentionally; two emails were found to be non-deliberative, and remedies were ordered.

allegations.summary: Committee members allegedly deliberated by email on public business (report to Town Meeting, fund balances, budget, warrant articles) among a quorum, April 25 to May 7, 2012.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the opinions, comments and revisions in Emails 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 should not have been shared with a quorum of the Committee's members outside of a properly posted open meeting.

allegations.summary: Email asking whether a prior email was received was alleged to be deliberation; the AG found it was purely administrative.
allegations.key_passage: We find that email 4, however, was not an improper deliberation because its content was limited to a purely administrative matter, namely whether a prior email was received.

allegations.summary: Email soliciting members to join a sign-holding demonstration was alleged to be deliberation; the AG found it was individual speech, not Committee business.
allegations.key_passage: Email 7 also was not an improper deliberation because it solicited Committee members to participate in a demonstration, which is considered a form of individual speech, rather than a matter of public business in the Committee's jurisdiction.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
All Committee members view the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law video training and certify in writing within 30 days that they have done so.
Publicly disclose the improper email communications at the Committee's next meeting.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. Additionally, we order the Committee to view the video training on the Open Meeting Law available at the Attorney General's website, and certify in writing to our office, within thirty (30) days after receiving this determination, that all of its members have done so. Finally, we order the Committee to publicly disclose the improper email communications at the Committee's next meeting.
